transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-28
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Maya (Cedar Springs CTO), Julian (PM), Elena (ML Eng)

Summary: quick hosted API demo focused on embeddings + reranking pipeline, walked through Console Optimize suggestions, discussed latency vs cost tradeoffs and pilot next steps. Customer asked about SOC2, data residency, and existing infra fit.

Topics covered:
- Hosted embeddings endpoint (vector encode)
- Reranker endpoint and two-stage retrieval + rerank flow
- Console: Evaluate + Optimize recommendations (batching, cache suggestions)
- Pilot scope, success metrics, security posture

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you taking the time. I'm Jordan Reed, AE at Redwood. Priya's gonna run the demo and I'll steer next steps. Maya, Julian, Elena, thanks for coming.
[00:00:12] Maya: Thanks, Jordan. Excited to see how the rerank flow can tighten our search results. We're trying to cut down MRR loss caused by bad matches.
[00:00:19] Priya: Awesome, quick agenda — first a short architecture sketch, then live through the hosted embeddings endpoint and the reranker API, then Console Optimize recommendations, then Q&A. Sound good?
[00:00:30] Julian: Yep, sounds great.
[00:00:33] Priya: So high-level we recommend a two-stage pipeline: 1) dense retrieval via embeddings — Redwood hosted embeddings endpoint, 2) rerank the top K with a higher-quality reranker model using Redwood's rerank endpoint. We'll show how to call both APIs and some Console workflows to tune thresholds.
[00:00:50] Elena: Quick q — can you clarify model latency for rerank? We're very sensitive, 200ms p95 or less ideally.
[00:00:57] Priya: Yeah, good call. For hosted, depending on model family and token length, standard rerank models hit p95 around 120–250ms for K=5 if you run single-token scoring paths; if you want sub-200ms consistently we recommend the smaller reranker variants or dedicated lanes. There's an Optimize suggestion that picks K and batch sizes to hit your SLOs at lower cost.
[00:01:20] Maya: When you say "dedicated lanes" do you mean Redwood Dedicated or some sort of reserved capacity?
[00:01:25] Jordan: Correct — Dedicated is reserved GPU pools. For predictable low p95 and higher QPS you can commit. For initial pilots hosted usually suffices and is faster to get started.
[00:01:36] Julian: How do we measure unit cost? We need to justify to finance.
[00:01:40] Priya: Console shows token-level cost and a per-request breakdown. We'll demo the Optimize tab which gives batching/caching recommendations and an estimated $/1000-requests metric. I'll pull that up now.
[00:01:50] [00:01:50] Priya: (screen share) Ok, this is Console — per-route latency, token cost, and an Optimize suggestion card. Here you'd upload sample queries and ground-truth labels or use live traffic for continuous evaluation. It will propose: reduce K to 8, or use prefix KV caching, or quantized model variant to lower cost while keeping NDCG above your threshold.
[00:02:20] Maya: We have a labeled set of ~2k queries, is that enough for Optimize to give useful suggestions?
[00:02:26] Priya: Yes, 2k is fine to start. Optimize will surface regressed examples and give concrete model + param suggestions. Important caveat: small samples can overfit, so we also recommend A/Bing with a holdout if you can.
[00:02:40] Elena: You mentioned KV cash — did you mean cache, KV cache?
[00:02:43] Priya: Sorry, yeah KV cache, my typo. That's the token-prefix cache we use to avoid re-computing identical prefixes for chat-like rerankers.
[00:02:53] [00:02:53] Jordan: Real quick architecture diagram slide — we support hosted endpoints via a single REST call. Example flow: POST /v1/embeddings -> store vectors in your vector DB -> when query comes, call /v1/search to get candidate ids -> call /v1/rerank with (query, topN candidates) — you can stream responses or get a single scored list.
[00:03:20] Julian: Can the rerank endpoint accept raw doc text or only ids and embeddings?
[00:03:24] Priya: It accepts either. For highest accuracy pass the document text (or a compressed context) alongside candidates. There is also an embeddings-only rerank path where we rerank purely on vector similarity. The text-aware reranker is usually better for precision.
[00:03:40] Maya: What about privacy — we can't send PII to hosted APIs for a subset of users. How do you handle that?
[00:03:47] Jordan: We get that a lot. Options: 1) Redwood Private — VPC or on-prem package; 2) Hosted but with strict retention: we support configurable retention windows and encryption at rest with customer-managed KMS. We also provide SOC 2 Type II artifacts and support SAML SSO for Console access.
[00:04:05] Elena: Is there support for field-level encryption or tokenization before vectorization?
[00:04:09] Priya: We have recommended patterns — you can tokenize or hash fields client-side, and we also support enclave-like KM integrations for key management. For full on-prem PII handling our Private deployment is the recommended path.
[00:04:22] [00:04:22] Julian: For evaluation, can we replay traffic into Optimize or run offline evaluations?
[00:04:27] Priya: Yes, both. You can upload queries + labels as a CSV or wire up a replay pipeline. Optimize runs offline evals and surfaces metrics like MRR, NDCG, latency, and cost impact of config changes.
[00:04:40] Maya: Show us an example API call please — the shape a few lines.
[00:04:43] Priya: Sure. (typing) POST /v1/embeddings {"input": "what is product return policy"} returns vector. Then POST /v1/rerank {"query":"what is product return policy", "candidates":[{"id":"123","text":"..."}, ...]} and you get scored list. Small example in SDK: redwood.rerank(query, candidates, model="rerank-small") — it returns scores.
[00:05:10] Maya: Are there SDKs for Python and node?
[00:05:13] Jordan: Yes, official SDKs: python, node, and a simple curl example.
[00:05:16] Elena: For throughput, what batching would you recommend if we have bursts at 200 QPS?
[00:05:21] Priya: For 200 QPS bursts, automatic batching in the runtime helps — Optimize will recommend a batch size that trades off latency vs GPU utilization. On hosted, we'll auto-scale, but for tight latency SLOs consider Dedicated. In practice we see a 30–40% cost savings with continuous batching and prefix caching on typical ecommerce traffic.
[00:05:42] [00:05:42] Julian: Any gotchas with vector DB integration? We're on Pinecone today.
[00:05:46] Priya: Pinecone, Weaviate, and Elastic are all common. You push embeddings to your chosen store; Redwood's search endpoint can return candidate ids plus metadata to fetch from your DB, or you can call embeddings locally and do all retrieval client-side. We can also provide small connectors / scripts as part of pilot.
[00:06:05] Maya: Competitors like X provide managed retriever+reranker bundles — why Redwood?
[00:06:10] Jordan: Two parts — performance predictability and operational tooling. Redwood focuses on production economics: powerful Optimize tooling, per-token cost visibility, and fallbacks between hosted and dedicated variants. We also have first-class rollouts and observability so you see exactly where regressions happen.
[00:06:26] Priya: And we tune kernels, batching, and quantization options under the hood; customers get recommendations that are implementable in minutes, not months.
[00:06:34] Elena: If we wanted a pilot, what's a minimal scope?
[00:06:38] Jordan: Typical pilot is 2–4 weeks: we ingest ~5k documents, run tuning against 2k labeled queries, run a 48-hour production-like benchmark with 1–2k synthetic QPS, and then deliver a results doc with proposed config and costs. We can do a paid pilot or apply credits depending on your ARR.
[00:06:56] [00:06:56] Julian: That fits our timeline. We're targeting an internal GA in Q4, so pilot now makes sense.
[00:07:02] Maya: Ok let's talk technical requirements for the pilot — what do you need from us?
[00:07:06] Priya: Sample dataset (5k docs), labeled queries (2k), and a brief success metric doc (target MRR uplift or reduction in false positives). Also we will need an IAM contact for SSO and a security engineer for SOC2 questions.
[00:07:20] Jordan: I'll add that to action items. We'll also share the security pack and the cost estimator spreadsheet.
[00:07:26] [00:07:26] Maya: One more: do you keep logs of the raw text by default? We want minimal retention.
[00:07:31] Priya: Default hosted retention is 30 days for debugging, but it's configurable; we can set it to zero persistent retention and only keep ephemeral logs for X hours. Also support bring-your-own-KMS for encryption.
[00:07:44] Elena: For evaluation we might want an internal reranker too — ability to plug custom model?
[00:07:48] Priya: You can bring your own reranker in Redwood Private. For hosted, we can host customer-provided models in Dedicated under contract, but not normally in the shared hosted fleet.
[00:08:00] [00:08:00] Jordan: Okay, wrapping up — quick recap of next steps. Priya will run a benchmark using your sample data and share a latency/cost spreadsheet. Jordan will send pricing tiers and a pilot SOW and the security pack. Maya will share anonymized logs and the labeled queries. We'll schedule a follow-up focused on Console Optimize deeper walkthrough.
[00:08:20] Maya: Thanks — that sounds actionable.
[00:08:23] Julian: One last question: any code examples for doing rerank in batch?
[00:08:27] Priya: Sure, we'll include a python snippet in the follow-up: chunk queries, call embeddings.batch_encode, then for each query call rerank with top candidates in batch mode — there's an SDK helper for vectorized rerank to avoid per-call overhead.
[00:08:42] Maya: Great. Appreciate the session everyone.
[00:08:45] Jordan: Thanks all, we'll follow up early next week.
